newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana governor calls for sales tax renewal.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana governor calls for sales tax renewal.

text.p: Louisiana Gov. Mike Foster called for renewal of a "temporary" one-cent sales tax on food and utilities in order to pay for education improvements and teacher pay raises.

In a speech Wednesday to Louisiana Assessors Association, Foster said he expected to release details by the end of next week on that proposal and others to be introduced in a special legislative session beginning Feb 23.
The sales tax is set to expire June 30 and generates $100 million a year.

Food and utilities were supposed to be exempt from the state's four-percent sales tax. But every year for at least the last decade, lawmakers have adopted "temporary" waivers allowing the state to keep collecting the tax.
Last year, lawmakers renewed three cents of the tax until June 30, 1998, but agreed to let one cent of the tax expire on June 30, 1997.

Foster said the state needs the extra cent for education. He also said it was unlikly the federal government would give Louisiana the extra money it has requested for Medicaid if the state gives up any of its own revenue sources.
Without the extra federal money, Louisiana will face a $400 million hole in its budget.
